description: The English wording of the step-label suite. A factor step carries its own label verbatim, regardless of language — this suite's factor case is genuinely language-independent, since stepLabel never inspects a factor's label, only echoes it. A unit step renders "<count> <unit>", pluralised by english-plural rather than french-plural. The key divergence from step-label.json: at count 0.25 and 0.5, French stays singular ("¼ carotte") while English pluralises ("¼ carrots") — english-plural's rule fires on both fractions, not just whole counts. Hand-authored: the sandbox stays French-only and has no English reference implementation to generate this from.
generatedBy: hand-authored — sandbox is out of scope, no reference implementation exists

cases.why: Factor steps are pre-labelled, so no formatting is applied — language-independent by construction.
A whole count renders as a digit, not a fraction, and stays singular — the one case English and French agree on.
Ties this suite to english-plural: the unit label is pluralised by that function, not by a second copy of the logic living here.
THE key divergence from French's "½ carotte": English's plural rule fires on 0.5 (anything but exactly 1), so this reads "½ carrots" even though the fraction glyph itself is the same one French uses.
The other fraction reachable from the anchor ladder — same divergence as the half case.
A count with no fraction entry falls back to the digit.
